title: 0.14.0: an ADR can link a decision id the way it links task ids
description: Operator-approved 0.14.0 item (opum-doc seq 179, ODOC-OP-2026-10-03-10, read verbatim on opum-agent OPAG-1094 at origin/dev 647473bd): (b) an ADR can link a decision id the way it links task ids. Design of record: opum-doc docs/reference/questions-decisions-and-adrs.md. Workers implement exactly this and report issues to opum-doc; they make no design calls. Filed 2026-10-03, not to be started until the 0.13.0 PR (opum-ai/lore-cli#476) is merged and the fleet restart is behind us.

acceptanceCriteria.text: An ADR links a decision id the way it links task ids: `lore link --decision <id>` writes repository-qualified `<repo>:DEC-N` entries to the concept's `decisions:` frontmatter (mirroring `tasks:`), document-side only. The qualifier resolves --repo > workspace member id > the origin remote's name > a refusal naming --repo. (The lore tasks-style rollup that CONSUMES these entries is LCLI-719, split out under DEC-193.)

implementationNotes:
PROBE (2026-10-14, branch feat/LCLI-670-adr-decision-id-link). Design of record read BY REF: opum-doc docs/reference/questions-decisions-and-adrs.md, section "Lore, built by lore-cli in 0.14.0".
WHAT EXISTS: the task machinery this mirrors is complete and clear — lore link <id> <taskId...> writes the concept's tasks: frontmatter list (src/commands/link.ts), and lore tasks <id> renders the linked tasks' LIVE status (src/commands/tasks.ts).
WHAT DOES NOT EXIST: any decision surface. No decision_id/decisions: frontmatter field (REF_FIELDS is only specs/supersedes/superseded_by), no decision arm on lore link, and no decision read in the tracker adapter.
SCOPE QUESTION (reported to opum-doc via the leader, NOT settled here): the record says an ADR can link a decision id "so lore tasks-style rollups CAN show the decision's state". Reading 1 = the LINK only (a frontmatter field plus the link arm), which enables the rollup. Reading 2 = also build the decision rollup, which needs a decision READ from the tracker that does not exist and whose shape (backend, a missing decision, tracker unavailable) the record does not specify. Recommendation: Reading 1 for this task, rollup as a follow-up. Implementation waits on the ruling.

STATUS (2026-10-14). The A/B this task waited on is RULED — DEC-192 (5), opum-ai/opum-doc#1011 — so the stale "waits on A/B" note was dropped rather than left to read as current. Implemented to that ruling: `lore link --decision <id>`, document-side only; qualifier order --repo > workspace member id > the origin remote's name > a refusal naming --repo; never the directory name.

Review round 1 (REQUEST CHANGES at a40a8041) addressed on this head: B1 dedupe the qualified ids case-insensitively BEFORE scoring; B2 guard the git spawn so a missing git binary is "no remote", not an uncaught exit 1; N3 the unlink refusal deleted as unreachable (unlink does not declare the flag, so the parser rejects it first — deleting was the smaller of the two options the reviewer offered); N4 the four refusal tests plus the answer on no-ids (it was exit 2 before this change and still is, so no CHANGELOG line); N5 the qualifier edge shapes (ownerless scp remote yields the name, a Windows path is refused); N6 an empty --repo refused; N7 the manifest summary fixed in BOTH sources plus a regenerated skills/lore/SKILL.md, and the cli-surface Output row names `decisions` and the empty `tasks`; N8 the [Unreleased] CHANGELOG entry; N9 `repeatable` on --decision.

LCLI-670 COMPLETION VERIFICATION (2026-10-14). The acceptance criterion was verified against origin/dev 157d57fa, not against the branch that built it.

WHAT LANDED, BY REF. PR opum-ai/lore-cli#581 MERGED 2026-10-14T09:38:04Z with head ref OID 432cf61b — the round-2 reviewed revision — squashed to 6ab1e32b, an ancestor of origin/dev. The round-2 follow-ups F11-F16 were filed on LCLI-727 and landed in opum-ai/lore-cli#588 (squash e9568455, also an ancestor of origin/dev); LCLI-727 is Done.

THE SQUASH CARRIES THE REVIEWED REVISION, measured: git diff 432cf61b 6ab1e32b -- src/ test/ .lore/ is EMPTY, so the merged content is that revision for every path the feature touches.

THE CRITERION, measured by RUNNING THE COMMAND on origin/dev code, which is byte-identical to the verifying checkout for those paths (git diff --stat origin/dev HEAD -- src/ .lore/schemas/ docs/reference/cli-surface.md skills/lore/SKILL.md is empty). The harness drove the real CLI (bun src/cli.ts, cwd = a temp bundle; the fixture writes the .git/config stanza rather than running git remote add). 13 checks, 13 pass: a bare DEC-9 with origin git@github.com:opum-ai/lore-cli.git writes decisions: [lore-cli:DEC-9] and exits 0; --repo opum-doc beats the remote; with no origin remote it exits 2, the refusal names --repo, and nothing is written; a bundle whose DIRECTORY name is a review-worktree name still qualifies from the remote; an already-qualified opum-doc:DEC-12 is kept as authored; a repeated --decision is ONE entry; and the --json result is data.decisions [{decision: lore-cli:DEC-9, status: added}], data.tasks [], backlogCommit {committed: false, files: []}.

DOC-SIDE ONLY, proved by construction rather than by absence: the run succeeds in a bundle with no tracker configured at all, and the payload carries no task id and no back-reference field.

THE MIDDLE ARM OF THE QUALIFIER ORDER. resolveDecisionQualifier encodes --repo > workspace member id > origin remote name > refusal naming --repo, and test/link-decision.test.ts covers the memberId arm; the arm has no caller because lore link operates on a bare bundle, which the resolver comment states and the sole caller confirms by passing only root and repoFlag. The order is implemented and tested at the resolution surface; the member-id arm is a resolver contract with no caller yet, not a missing behaviour.

test/link-decision.test.ts on this head: 29 pass / 2 skip / 0 fail, both skips being the runtime case-sensitivity probe named in the test title, because macOS APFS cannot hold two names differing only by case.
finalSummary: lore link --decision <id> links a decision id the way a task id is linked: a repository-qualified <repo>:DEC-N entry in the concept decisions: frontmatter, doc-side only, with no tracker back-reference and a bare DEC-N qualified from --repo > workspace member id > the origin remote name > a refusal naming --repo. Delivered in opum-ai/lore-cli#581 (head 432cf61b, squash 6ab1e32b, MERGED 2026-10-14); its round-2 follow-ups F11-F16 landed under LCLI-727 in opum-ai/lore-cli#588 (squash e9568455). Verified 2026-10-14 against origin/dev 157d57fa by running the real CLI in temp bundles — 13 of 13 checks pass, covering the remote-derived qualifier, --repo precedence, the refusal naming --repo, an authored qualifier, dedupe, and the doc-side-only payload — with test/link-decision.test.ts at 29 pass / 2 skip / 0 fail, both skips being the runtime case-sensitivity probe. The task was still In Progress only because its completion was never written down; no code changed here.
